title: FDE, ML engineer, research engineer, platform — what actually differs day to day?
body:
These titles overlap heavily and the job postings are near-identical, which makes it hard to tell
what you are actually interviewing for.

My read, from the shape of the interview loops rather than the postings:

| Role | The loop tests | The day is mostly |
|---|---|---|
| **Forward-deployed / deployment engineer** | ambiguity, stakeholders, sequencing — *"what is week one?"* | figuring out what the client actually needs, then building the smallest thing that proves it |
| **ML engineer** | the mechanism, and whether you can measure it | pipelines, evaluation, and the gap between offline and online |
| **Research engineer** | falsification — *"design the experiment that would disprove this"* | making somebody else's result reproduce, and finding out why it does not |
| **Platform / infra** | scale, failure modes, cost | the 69% of the bill that is not tokens |

The [interview sheets](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/blob/main/docs/60-cheatsheets/interviews/navigating-the-loop.md) go
further on what each round scores.

### What I want from this thread

**Correct me.** If you hold one of these titles, what does the table get wrong? The most useful
reply is the boring detail — what you spend Tuesday morning on.
